sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Chemical Fractionation of Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin Crude

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: OECD Mutual Assistance Convention (multilateral treaty for tax cooperation)
France-Benelux and EU Treaty framework on freedom of establishment
France-China Investment Protection Agreement 2007 (representative BIT for foreign shareholders)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (French Monetary and Financial Code), Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq. as amended; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 (transposition of EU Directive 2018/843); Code de commerce, Article L.561-2-2 (RBE register); Décret n° 2021-868 of 29 June 2021; EU Regulation 2015/847 on the transfer of funds.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled or consular legalized copy of passport/identity document of each shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the shareholder's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961) where applicable; otherwise consular legalization by the French embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate extract of any legal-person shareholder, with apostille and certified translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company's registry or competent trade registrar

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) for non-resident signatories, duly apostilled or legalized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or equivalent public authority in the shareholder's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all non-French documents (articles, passports, corporate instruments) by a court-registered translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Expert translator registered with the Cour de Cassation or a Court of Appeal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required if translated by the certified translator; notarial certification may be required by the Greffe in certain cases

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against: (i) French national asset-freeze and financial sanctions lists (DG Trésor); (ii) EU consolidated restrictive measures lists; (iii) UN Security Council sanctions; (iv) OFAC and UK sanctions lists where USD or UK nexus exists; and (v) French national PEP database under Article L.561-10 CMF. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs; any positive hit must be escalated immediately and may trigger a Suspicious Activity Report to Tracfin under Article L.561-15 CMF. A clean AML/KYC checkpoint is a condition precedent to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises of INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); preliminary name search via Infogreffe registry portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must comply with the French Language Act (Loi Toubon) and may include foreign terms only if they are capable of a clear French transliteration or are French-accepted. The name must not be deceptive, unlawful, or contrary to public order (Article R.123-53 of the Code de commerce). The entity must use the suffix 'SAS'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tolerated only with prior ministerial or sectorial approval; certain medical terms require a formal authorisation from the pharmaceutical regulator
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In France there is no administrative pre-reservation of a corporate name. If the RCS registrar (Greffe) rejects the filing due to the name, the burden falls on the applicant to publish an amendment. The applicant may appeal the registrar's refusal before the judge charged with supervision of the RCS (juge chargé du suivi du registre du commerce et des sociétés) within 10 days of notification. Alternatively, the applicant may refile the M0 form with an amended name. Conflicts with prior rights may be challenged before the civil courts under trademark law; no administrative extension of validity is available for a non-reserved name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. At incorporation stage, a commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) is allowed under Article L.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce, provided it has a physical registered address in France where official mail is received. However, for an active heparin sodium extraction and pharmaceutical manufacturing operation, the operating company must also maintain physical operational, GMP-compliant, quality-control, and logistics premises in France or the EU; the registered office cannot be the only place of commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High (approximately 60–75% within the first 24 months), due to the active pharmaceutical ingredient classification, the medium-risk enhanced AML tier, and applicable GMP inspection by ANSM under Article L.5136-1 of the French Public Health Code.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company registration and RCS filing fees (guichet unique and registry annexes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce via INPI

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the statutory notice of incorporation (avis de constitution) in a licensed legal announcement gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated advertising rates for legal notices (tarif des annonces légales)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and review of the articles of association (statuts) by a French avocat or notaire
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee for SAS incorporation, plus notarial tariff if notarized

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification, AML/KYC, PEP, OFAC, EU/UN and French asset-freeze screening for all directors, shareholders and beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for enhanced due diligence on medium-risk pharmaceutical structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, consular legalization, and certified French translation of foreign corporate and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French consulate / apostille authority in the document's country of origin / court-certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule and translator benchmark rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Capital deposit and pre-opening bank account attestation (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank or notarial tariff for issued capital blocking certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Regulatory pre-incorporation assessment of heparin sodium active substance licensure with ANSM (pharma legal feasibility)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for pharmaceutical regulatory due diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, including Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. governing sociétés par actions simplifiées; Articles L.210-1 to L.210-9 and R.210-1 et seq. governing commercial companies; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. governing the Trade and Companies Register; and Articles L.561-46 et seq. governing beneficial-owner filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The National Register of Enterprises is administered through the INPI electronic one-stop shop (Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises); the relevant Trade and Companies Register is maintained by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of company formation submitted through the INPI Guichet unique, including the applicable company-creation form and beneficial-owner declaration, supported by the signed SAS articles of association and required evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon subscription, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash may be deposited into a blocked account with a bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the deposit certificate supports registration and funds are released after presentation of the Kbis extract. In-kind contributions must be fully contributed and may require a commissaire aux apports report, subject to statutory exemptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept and record the subscriptions for the shares specified in the articles of association and acknowledge receipt of the required paid-in cash contributions. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full French address] and remain there until lawfully changed. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Président for the term and authority specified in the articles, and that [name(s)] be appointed Directeur Général(s), if applicable. RESOLVED, that the Président is authorized to complete all INPI, Trade and Companies Register, tax, banking, beneficial-owner, employment, pharmaceutical, environmental, and premises formalities necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate structure, shareholders, and regulated business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique preparatory portal; legal review with the competent commercial court registry, ANSM, and DREAL where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SAS shareholder structure, French registered office, share capital, share classes, Président, any Directeur Général, fiscal option, beneficial owners, and precise activities. Separate pharmaceutical active-substance manufacturing from trading, importation, warehousing, and medicinal-product manufacture because each may trigger different authorizations. Obtain written premises and activity classification before signing the final operating lease.
required_dossiers: Corporate shareholder certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents
Business activity description and ISIC/NACE classification
Draft pharmaceutical, environmental, and premises compliance matrix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the scope, NAF/NACE classification, ownership information, or premises evidence before filing. Obtain written pre-consultation from ANSM or DREAL where the activity classification is uncertain.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Depositary bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the articles of association and subscription documents. Open the capital-deposit account, transfer the subscribed cash contributions, and obtain the certificate of deposit. Ensure the articles identify the share capital, contributions, management powers, decision rules, transfer restrictions, and statutory auditor provisions where applicable. Foreign corporate documents should be apostilled or legalized when required and accompanied by certified French translations.
required_dossiers: Share subscription forms or equivalent subscription evidence
Identification and powers of attorney for depositors
Apostilled or legalized foreign documents and French translations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank or notary compliance queries with ownership, source-of-funds, and corporate-authority evidence. Replace defective signatures or contribution documents and obtain a corrected deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-notice publication service in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the statutory incorporation notice in an authorized journal or authorized online legal-notice service. The notice must state the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, term, management arrangements, and registration details required by the French Commercial Code. Retain the publication certificate for the INPI filing.
required_dossiers: Final articles or incorporation data sheet
Président and other mandatory management particulars
Legal-notice publication order and payment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or republication if the notice contains an omission or discrepancy. Upload the corrected publication certificate and maintain an audit trail of both publications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic company-formation declaration, articles, registered-office evidence, publication certificate, capital deposit certificate, management identification, non-conviction and parentage declarations where required, beneficial-owner filing, and foreign-document evidence. The authorized representative must sign electronically and pay the applicable registry charges. The INPI transmits the file to the relevant commercial court registry and other administrations.
required_dossiers: Corporate shareholder documents and powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI dashboard and respond within the stated deadline to any request for regularization. Upload replacement documents in the requested format, pay any additional charge, and resubmit without changing the filing reference unless instructed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration and activate post-registration records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry, INPI, tax administration, and Banque de France or banking institution as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers, provide the Kbis to the depositary bank to release capital, open operational bank accounts, and verify registration with the tax and social-security administrations. Maintain the beneficial-owner record and establish accounting, invoicing, payroll, electronic VAT, and statutory-register controls. Register the establishment separately if the manufacturing site differs from the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Escalate delayed or rejected registration to the competent commercial court registry through the INPI support channel. Correct tax, social, or beneficial-owner inconsistencies immediately and preserve evidence of all submissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish pharmaceutical quality and active-substance compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM); European Medicines Agency where an EU centralized procedure is relevant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the site manufactures an active substance, an intermediate, a medicinal product, or an imported product. Implement applicable EU Good Manufacturing Practice, quality-system, batch-release, traceability, supplier-qualification, deviation, CAPA, validation, contamination-control, and data-integrity procedures. File any required ANSM declaration, authorization, establishment registration, or variation before commercial manufacture or supply. Do not market material as a medicinal product without the relevant marketing authorization and manufacturing authorization.
required_dossiers: Responsible-person and qualified-person evidence, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to ANSM deficiency letters with a dated remediation plan, revised procedures, objective evidence, and effectiveness checks. Suspend affected operations where required and do not commence regulated manufacture before the applicable authorization or registration is effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain ICPE environmental authorization or declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Prefect of the department through the regional environment, planning and housing directorate (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement; DREAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Map all site activities against the French ICPE nomenclature, including chemical processing, solvent use, storage of hazardous substances, wastewater discharge, air emissions, waste storage, and pressure equipment. File the applicable authorization, registration, or declaration through the relevant environmental procedure. Install monitoring, secondary containment, emergency controls, waste traceability, and operating procedures before commissioning.
required_dossiers: Chemical inventory and safety data sheets
Water, air, waste, noise, and accident-risk assessments
Environmental impact or examination dossier, if required
Hazard study and emergency response plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to DREAL or prefectural requests within the prescribed period, amend the dossier, and address public-inquiry or inspection findings. Do not operate a classified installation before the required authorization, registration, or declaration status is effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete construction, fire, workplace, and commissioning clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality, departmental fire and rescue service (Service départemental d'incendie et de secours; SDIS), labor authorities, occupational health service, and relevant inspection bodies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain planning and building approvals where works or change of use require them. Commission fire detection, suppression, hazardous-material storage, evacuation, access, and emergency-response systems. Complete structural, electrical, pressure-equipment, ventilation, machine-safety, and workplace risk assessments. Consult the SDIS and occupational physician before opening and maintain the required health-and-safety register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies identified during inspection, obtain reinspection, and document corrective actions. Delay opening or restrict affected areas until fire, structural, occupational, and equipment-safety requirements are satisfied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No single industrial licensing board applies. The competent authorities are the Prefect of the department, assisted by DREAL for ICPE authorization, registration, or declaration; ANSM for applicable pharmaceutical establishment and active-substance compliance; and the municipality and SDIS for premises and fire-safety matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Site-specific ICPE environmental authorization, registration, or declaration (autorisation environnementale, enregistrement, or déclaration ICPE), together with any applicable ANSM pharmaceutical establishment authorization or active-substance manufacturing declaration/registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: French Ministry for Ecological Transition, acting through the Prefect and DREAL, with the competent environmental authority under the French Environmental Code
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site- and process-dependent: full environmental impact assessment, case-by-case examination, or exemption under Articles L.122-1 and R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code; the applicable ICPE regime may be authorization, registration, or declaration under the ICPE nomenclature.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable prefectural order and ICPE requirements for wastewater, hazardous substances, air emissions, VOCs, odors, noise, soil and groundwater protection, waste classification, storage, transport, and disposal. Apply EU industrial-emissions and BAT requirements where applicable. No universal project-wide numeric threshold applies; limits are set by the relevant ICPE regime, receiving environment, process capacity, and permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain required building and premises approvals, SDIS fire-safety review or opinion, emergency-access and evacuation compliance, fire detection and suppression certification, hazardous-material storage controls, and electrical and pressure-equipment inspections. Complete the French occupational-risk assessment document, chemical-exposure controls, machine and ventilation conformity, employee training, occupational-health arrangements, and workplace-opening notifications or consultations required for the site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the online portal impots.gouv.fr; business registration is administered through the Répertoire National des Entreprises (RNE) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an SAS incorporated in France, statutory identifiers (SIREN, SIRET, SIRENE registration) are obtained automatically at incorporation via the formalities portal. Corporate income tax registration is automatic with the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE). A separate French VAT identification number (n° d'identification TVA intracommunautaire) is issued by DGFiP after notification of the SIREN; a distinct EORI number is required for customs purposes only if the entity undertakes customs operations. Foreign entities carrying on taxable supplies in France without a permanent establishment must register directly with DGFiP under the non-resident simplified VAT registration procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The SAS is a capital company (société de capitaux) and is irrebuttably subject to French corporate income tax (IS) at the entity level; no pass-through treatment is available. Territorial scope applies to foreign permanent establishments unless a worldwide group election is made.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not offer a US-style 'check-the-box' election. Available elections include: (i) option for tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) for a 95%+ French parent; (ii) election for the régime des sociétés mères (parent-subsidiary dividend exemption); (iii) election for VAT grouping (assujettis unis); (iv) election to waive VAT exemption on qualifying leased property. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD 1 and 2 apply per CGI Article 212 bis and impose entity characterization based on foreign law, but no separate hybrid election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for established businesses: any French SAS supplying goods or services must be VAT-registered from inception. For non-established EU suppliers, an annual distance-selling threshold of €35,000 applies to goods sold to French consumers; for non-EU suppliers, no threshold applies once a taxable supply occurs (importation is always taxable).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is transitioning to mandatory electronic invoicing under the 2020 Finance Act: all established businesses must be able to receive e-invoices by 1 July 2026 and issue e-invoices by 1 July 2026 (large enterprises) and 1 January 2027 (SMEs). Invoices are transmitted through certified Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDP) or the public portal Chorus Pro. No real-time fiscal stamping is required; however, a real-time 'e-reporting' data transmission of transaction data to DGFiP is mandatory. Customs exports are cleared electronically via the DELTA system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to a destination outside the EU are zero-rated for French VAT under CGI Article 262-I. The supplier must prove that the goods physically left EU territory within 90 days of dispatch. Services directly related to exported goods (e.g., loading, transport, handling) may also be zero-rated under Article 262-II. For pharmaceutical products, export zero-rating is unconditional on the nature of the goods, provided the export is genuine and documented. The export must occur under customs control, evidenced by an accepted customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document – DAU via DELTA)
Commercial invoice meeting VAT invoicing requirements
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) with carrier and shipping dates
Proof of international transport (CMR note, railway bill, etc.)
Evidence of exit from the EU customs territory (customs exit confirmation)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT proof of payment for the exported goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or insufficiently documented export zero-rating triggers: (i) immediate VAT clawback plus 0.40% monthly late payment interest; (ii) 50% penalty for lack of bona fide provided documentation and 80% penalty for intentional concealment or abusive situations; (iii) criminal penalties under CGI Article 1741 (five years imprisonment and €500,000 fine); (iv) retrospective reassessment within a six-year statute of limitation. DGFiP audits export proofs strictly and requires consistent documentation between customs declarations, commercial contracts, and payment flows.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange policy is governed principally by European Union and euro-area rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general exchange control over current-account or capital-account transactions. The SAS may generally receive foreign capital, convert currencies, pay suppliers, remit dividends, repay shareholder funding, and transfer liquidation proceeds, subject to bank anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax, customs, foreign-investment-screening, and beneficial-ownership controls. Dividend and other profit remittances require distributable profits, approved financial statements, corporate approvals, and compliance with applicable French withholding tax, treaty, or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions. Cross-border capital movements involving sanctioned persons, restricted jurisdictions, controlled goods, or regulated pharmaceutical materials may be blocked or require governmental authorization. Certain foreign-investment transactions in strategic pharmaceutical activities may require prior French screening or notification, depending on the investor, activity, control rights, and transaction structure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a domestic bank, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline for converting export receipts. Export proceeds may remain in euros or foreign currency, subject to contractual banking arrangements, accounting, tax, customs, sanctions, and transaction-reporting obligations. Banks may request invoices, customs declarations, transport documents, end-customer information, and an economic-purpose explanation before crediting or converting funds. The company must preserve records supporting export, VAT, customs, transfer-pricing, and payment compliance. Cross-border cash movements and certain statistical or balance-of-payments information may be reportable under applicable French, European Union, or Banque de France frameworks.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account for SAS incorporation or capital increase, plus operational current account and foreign-currency accounts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account for SAS incorporation or capital increase, plus operational current account and trade-finance facilities
Capital deposit account, operational current account, foreign-currency account, and documentary-trade account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Groupe BPCE, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne entities
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account or operational account, subject to the selected legal entity's acceptance policy

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale or the relevant Crédit Mutuel local entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account and operational current account, subject to local entity onboarding and sector appetite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment accounts and international collections; low to medium for regulated pharmaceutical trade, capital-deposit functionality, documentary letters of credit, and complex treasury. An EU electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, SEPA transfers, foreign-exchange execution, and selected international payment services, but it is not equivalent to a French credit institution and may not accept statutory SAS share capital deposits, provide credit, issue all forms of commercial letters of credit, or support every SWIFT and correspondent-banking service. The EMI must be authorized under the applicable EU passporting framework, conduct full KYC and beneficial-owner verification, apply sanctions and transaction monitoring, and comply with safeguarding requirements. Offshore non-EU digital EMIs may require an EU or French authorization, local regulated partner, or reliance on a permitted cross-border-services regime. The SAS should maintain a regulated French or EU bank as its primary account for capital, payroll, taxes, regulated trade, and contingency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that every director physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available for an SAS where the bank accepts qualified electronic identification and documentary verification. Banks may nevertheless require a physical meeting, live video interview, certified documents, French-resident contact, notarized or apostilled corporate records, or an in-person visit because of non-resident ownership, complex ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, pharmaceutical activity, foreign-currency flows, trade-finance requests, or enhanced-risk classification. The legal representative and all ultimate beneficial owners must be identified and verified; authorized signatories and relevant controllers may also be interviewed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain, nominee shareholder, unidentified ultimate beneficial owner, or unexplained control rights.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership and control chart to the natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; passports and address evidence; board or shareholder resolutions; powers of attorney; and a signed beneficial-ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, foreign parent, politically exposed person, close associate, or connection to a sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full group organizational chart; certified corporate registry extracts; tax-residency evidence; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; PEP screening results; sanctions-screening evidence; bank statements; audited accounts; transaction rationale; and documented enhanced-monitoring controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Active-pharmaceutical extraction or heparin-related activity without clear licensing, product classification, manufacturing, import, export, quality, or distribution permissions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; precise product and substance descriptions; applicable French and EU pharmaceutical, chemical, customs, and environmental permits; manufacturing or distribution authorizations; Good Manufacturing Practice or equivalent quality documentation where applicable; supplier and customer profiles; batch, origin, and traceability procedures; and confirmation that controlled biological materials are lawfully sourced and transported.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source or provenance of heparin crude material, animal-derived inputs, or payments involving jurisdictions exposed to supply-chain, corruption, sanctions, or traceability concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier due-diligence files; beneficial-owner checks; origin certificates; veterinary, sanitary, and customs documents; transport records; purchase contracts; invoices; quality certificates; chain-of-custody records; import authorizations; adverse-media screening; and a risk-based supplier approval policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-value cross-border transfers inconsistent with the stated business model or lacking an identifiable commercial counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year financial model; expected monthly transaction profile; countries and currencies involved; customer and supplier lists; executed contracts; purchase orders; invoices; customs and shipping documents; payment-flow diagram; expected payment purposes; and written reconciliation procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for cash, third-party payments, personal accounts, rapid pass-through transfers, split payments, or payments to unrelated jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy prohibiting cash and unauthorized third-party payments; approved-signatory matrix; payment approval workflow; segregation-of-duties policy; reconciliation controls; counterparty bank-account verification; exception-approval records; and documented commercial justification for any permitted third-party settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax, customs, transfer-pricing, VAT, or beneficial-ownership inconsistencies between bank information and public or regulatory filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax registration; VAT number; customs registration where applicable; tax-residency certificates; annual accounts; management accounts; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; customs classification analysis; VAT compliance evidence; and reconciliations between accounting ledgers, invoices, customs declarations, and bank statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficiently documented capital injection, shareholder loan, acquisition funding, or repatriation of profits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital subscription agreement; shareholder or board resolutions; capital-deposit certificate request; executed shareholder-loan agreement; funding-source evidence; bank statements; financial statements; dividend resolution; proof of distributable reserves; withholding-tax analysis; and evidence of treaty or EU relief where claimed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, litigation, insolvency, regulatory action, or compliance concerns involving the SAS, directors, shareholders, suppliers, or customers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal memorandum; court and registry searches; explanation of each matter; settlement or remediation evidence; compliance-program documentation; audited financial information; regulatory correspondence; and updated sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media screening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscribed share capital to a French bank's dedicated capital-deposit account in the name of the company being incorporated or recapitalized. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro funding within SEPA or SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-SEPA currencies. The payment narrative should identify the SAS, subscriber, capital increase or incorporation, subscription amount, and corporate reference. Provide the bank with the subscription agreement, draft or executed articles, shareholder and board resolutions, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, and transfer-pricing or shareholder-loan documentation where relevant. After receipt, obtain the bank capital-deposit certificate and complete registration or capital-increase formalities before releasing funds to the operational account. For a shareholder loan, use a separately documented loan agreement and classify the transfer as debt funding rather than equity. There is no single universal French purpose-code regime equivalent to systems used in certain exchange-control jurisdictions; the bank may nevertheless require an internal payment purpose, SWIFT purpose information, invoice or contract reference, and economic-purpose evidence. Screen all parties, banks, countries, goods, and vessels against applicable EU and French sanctions before execution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer where available for euro payments to eligible beneficiaries. Use SWIFT MT103 for legacy cross-border customer credit transfers, with ISO 20022 pacs.008 increasingly used through bank migration; include complete originator, beneficiary, bank, invoice, goods, and purpose information. For heparin inputs, pharmaceutical materials, equipment, and international sales, use documentary letters of credit issued or confirmed by an acceptable bank under UCP 600, with eUCP where agreed; require compliant commercial invoices, packing lists, transport documents, certificates of origin, insurance documents, inspection or quality certificates, and applicable sanitary, veterinary, customs, or pharmaceutical permits. Documentary collections may use URC 522 where credit risk is acceptable. Establish dual approval, sanctions screening, beneficiary-account verification, invoice-to-contract matching, three-way matching, segregation of duties, and post-payment reconciliation. Do not use personal accounts, unapproved third-party beneficiaries, or payment routes designed to bypass sanctions, customs, tax, or bank controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or permitted investment firm, documented against forecast or contracted receivables, payables, capital contributions, or other identifiable exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency, counterparty, jurisdiction, product, and settlement structure are legally permitted and the instrument is used for genuine commercial exposure rather than speculative activity.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for documented medium- or long-term funding or liquidity exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval and appropriate collateral and termination provisions.
Foreign-exchange options or collars may be used where approved by the bank and treasury policy, with clear disclosure of premium, barrier, leverage, early-termination, and maximum-loss features.

Hedging documentation should address EMIR reporting, clearing or margin requirements where applicable, MiFID-related product governance, counterparty eligibility, ISDA or equivalent master documentation, confirmations, valuation, collateral, accounting designation, board limits, and periodic effectiveness testing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval decision by shareholders (SAS décision collective / written resolution, rapport de gestion if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders / SAS governance body; decision recorded in the statutory minutes book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year end (calendar-year SAS: by 30 June of the following year); compliance under Article L.232-23 Code de commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order obtainable by any interested party compelling approval or regularization; management liability and unavailability of filing may trigger tax and registry penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements with the commercial court registry (dépôt des comptes annuels, liasse comptable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval and in all cases within the seven months following the balance-sheet date; calendar-year SAS files by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,500 per annual account (Article R.123-110-7 Code de commerce), court-ordered penalty payment (astreinte), and repeated default leading to strike-off from the RCS (radiation d'office)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard 25% rate; R&D tax credit (crédit d'impôt recherche) up to 5% of eligible R&D expenses with €100 million cap; accelerated depreciation allowances; SME reduced rate of 15% for turnover below €50,000

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200 (Déclaration de résultat) via impots.gouv.fr electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the fourth month following fiscal year-end (e.g. 15 April for 31 December fiscal year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source turnover for non-resident entities

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for French deductibility rules and permanent differences
Apply treaty-based adjustments and transfer pricing corrections

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 0.5% of annual turnover per month of delay, capped at 5% of turnover or €75,000; criminal prosecution for willful evasion with fines up to 80% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% flat-rate withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-residents
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and completed form 3 277 to French tax authorities for reduced treaty rate application
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0%–10% depending on treaty (standard 5%); Interest: 0%–15% depending on treaty (standard 10% for related-party debt)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million consolidated turnover triggering Master File / Local File requirements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies Economic Substance Regulations for certain holding, IP holding and finance entities; active pharmaceutical manufacturing operations generally satisfy substance requirements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or submission of false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty: fines up to 80% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, plus civil restitution and disqualification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment, fines and possible travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation or use of non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to €100,000 per infringement; potential corporate tax reassessment and double taxation adjustment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several civil liability for unpaid tax plus possible criminal sanctions for fraudulent conduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining a French entity solely for tax residence without genuine commercial activity or substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation as non-resident, denial of all deductions and penalties up to 80% of tax benefit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for fraudulent tax evasion, disqualification from corporate offices and potential imprisonment
